crossRefs.note: For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as idolatry and teraphim. Because you have rejected…
If you are willing and obedient, you will eat the good of the land;
but if you refuse and rebel, you will be devoured with the sword; for the mouth of Yahweh has spoken it.”
Men will clap their hands at him, and will hiss him out of his place.
“How long will you speak these things? Shall the words of your mouth be a mighty wind?
Does God pervert justice? Or does the Almighty pervert righteousness?
“Shouldn’t the multitude of words be answered? Should a man full of talk be justified?
Should your boastings make men hold their peace? When you mock, will no man make you ashamed?
“Do you think this to be your right, or do you say, ‘My righteousness is more than God’s,’
that you ask, ‘What advantage will it be to you? What profit will I have, more than if I had sinned?’
Therefore Job opens his mouth with empty talk, and he multiplies words without knowledge.”
It was so, that after Yahweh had spoken these words to Job, Yahweh said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is kindled…

translations.web: For he adds rebellion to his sin. He claps his hands among us, and multiplies his words against God.”
translations.bsb: For he adds rebellion to his sin; he claps his hands among us and multiplies his words against God.”
